content.title: About
content.content: Onions are a bulbous plant of the Amaryllidaceae family cultivated for its edible bulbs. The bulbs have a sharp aroma, mildly sweet flavor and a crisp texture. Onions are eaten raw, sautéed, caramelized, and used as a base for sauces, soups, and sandwiches.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Onions were domesticated over 5,000 years ago in Central Asia.
There are more than 600 onion varieties, including yellow, red, white, and shallot.
Each layer of the bulb is a modified leaf.
Tearing is caused by volatile sulfur compounds released when the onion tissue is cut.
Onions can be stored in a cool, dry place for up to six months.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Onions contain quercetin and sulfur compounds that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Flavonoids and potassium in onions contribute to lower blood pressure and improved lipid profiles.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: Vitamin C and sulfur enhance immune cell function.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Fiber and prebiotic compounds promote the growth of beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Helps regulate blood sugar
items.content: Sulfur compounds may improve insulin sensitivity.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to onions, manifested as skin rashes or swelling.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: Large amounts of raw onion can cause heartburn or discomfort in people with high gastric acidity.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Sulfur compounds may enhance the effect of anticoagulants, so moderation is advised for those on blood thinners.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Onions can be used raw in salads and sandwiches, sautéed, caramelized, roasted, or added to soups and sauces. For a milder taste, lightly sauté the onion until golden.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store onions in a cool, dry, well‑ventilated area. Avoid sealed plastic bags to prevent moisture buildup. Discard any onions with mold or soft spots.
